body:
## Protocol preregistered; Issue #36's 24-movie artifacts are being consumed, not re-run

Branch [`feat/issue-61-scientific-noninferiority`](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/tree/feat/issue-61-scientific-noninferiority). The protocol was committed **before** any endpoint value was computed for any arm, at `0693c28`: [PROTOCOL.md](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/feat/issue-61-scientific-noninferiority/docs/issue61_noninferiority/PROTOCOL.md), with the architecture note at [`agents/designs/issue_61_scientific_noninferiority.md`](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/feat/issue-61-scientific-noninferiority/agents/designs/issue_61_scientific_noninferiority.md). No `src/`, comparator or threshold change is in scope.

**Inputs consumed.** Issue #36's full 24-movie three-arm run completed on 2026-09-25 (`cpu` on `cpu64`, `default` and `allfftw` on `4GPUs` GPU 0, source `5407373`, one movie per process, seed 1, `--dose_weighting --patch_x 5 --patch_y 5 --bfactor 150`). All 72 corrected micrographs verified present, identical geometry (3710x3838, mode 2, 0.885 A/pixel), and no accelerated arm bit-identical to CPU. Pixel-payload and core-header digests are recorded separately because the MRC label region carries a `strftime` timestamp.

**Design.** Three real arms plus three instrument controls, each in its own RELION project where only the `MotionCorr/job002/Movies/*.mrc` symlink target differs, so every downstream command is byte-identical across arms. Downstream matching comes from this dataset's own RELION 5.0 tutorial precalculated project: the same 24 micrographs, 4452 particles, imported orientations, CTF, half-set assignment, mask, box and symmetry. Unit of replication is the **movie**, never the pixel.

Prespecified margins, all derived before results — `pi/8` CTF phase error at 3.0 A (45 A defocus); 3% of the reference CTF-max-resolution mean (0.10 A); 5% effective-particle loss on a Rosenthal-Henderson basis for the primary reconstruction endpoint. Development set is `00021` + `00046` (they carried all of #36's diagnostics); the other **22 movies are held out**.

**Stage A (CTF / high-frequency screen) is complete** — 24 micrographs x 6 arms, CTFFIND 4.1 with the tutorial's own search parameters. On the 22 held-out movies, paired BCa bootstrap over movies:

| arm | CtfMaxResolution, A (margin +0.10) | mean defocus, A (margin +/-45) | CtfFoM, relative (margin -5%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | -0.0188, upper 95% bound **+0.0017** | -2.6, 90% CI [-10.5, -0.0] | +0.42%, lower bound -0.000 |
| `allfftw` | -0.0226, upper 95% bound **+0.0020** | -2.1, 90% CI [-9.4, +0.5] | +0.44%, lower bound +0.000 |

All six Stage A tests PASS non-inferiority on the held-out set, and the all-24 values agree. The instrument controls behave as designed: adding noise at 20% of micrograph variance **fails** the CTF figure-of-merit endpoint (-12.7%, bound -13.7%), and at 5% it lands at -3.5% — so this endpoint demonstrably responds to a known, quantified signal loss rather than being green by construction.

**Descriptive covariate**, from #36's own comparator output on the same 24 movies (not my verdict, and no threshold is evaluated here): `default` relative image RMSE median 0.00716 (24/24 FAIL); `allfftw` median 0.00110, range 0.00046-0.00302, **12 PASS / 12 FAIL** at the unchanged 0.001 limit. The two-movie hybrid result was therefore optimistic relative to the full set, which is consistent with what this issue asked to avoid.

**In progress:** Stage B, the matched-orientation controlled diagnostic — 156 `relion_reconstruct` jobs (6 arms x 2 half sets, plus a delete-one-movie jackknife over the 22 held-out movies for the three real arms), then `relion_postprocess` for half-map FSC and auto-B. Stage C, an independent auto-refinement per arm, follows if an uncontended GPU window holds.

**Coordination.** All work is under `docs/issue61_noninferiority/` and `agents/designs/issue_61_*`; I am not touching `docs/reference_gates.md` (#58), synthetic-truth fixtures (#59) or perturbation tooling (#60). Compute is on `4GPUs` under top-level `taskset -c 96-103` and `/tmp/motioncorr-bench.lock`, one phase at a time. Cross-host staging to `cpu64` measured 0.66 MB/s, which is why the 2.7 GB of accelerated-arm artifacts stayed where they were produced; RELION 5.1.0-commit-cb2683 is byte-identical on both hosts.

## Result: both accelerated backends are non-inferior in recoverable signal on the 22 held-out movies

Full report, exact commands and machine-readable results: **[PR #65](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/65)** → [`docs/issue61_noninferiority/README.md`](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/feat/issue-61-scientific-noninferiority/docs/issue61_noninferiority/README.md). The protocol was committed at `0693c28` before any endpoint value existed for any arm; nothing in `src/`, the comparator, or any threshold was changed.

### Verdicts (held-out 22 movies; one-sided 95%, TOST at 90% for A2)

| Stage | Endpoint | Margin, fixed in advance | `default` | `allfftw` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | CtfMaxResolution | +0.10 A | PASS (-0.019, bound +0.002) | PASS (-0.023, bound +0.002) |
| A | mean defocus | +/- 45 A | PASS (-2.6 A) | PASS (-2.1 A) |
| A | CtfFigureOfMerit | -5% rel. | PASS (+0.42%) | PASS (+0.44%) |
| **B** | **effective-data fraction `rho` vs CPU** | **>= 0.95** | **PASS, >= 0.99969** | **PASS, >= 0.99992** |
| B | `d143` delta | <= +0.05 A | INCONCLUSIVE (point 0.000 A) | PASS (0.000 A) |
| B | auto-B delta | >= -10 A^2 | PASS | PASS |
| C | `d143`, independent auto-refinement | <= +0.05 A | PASS | PASS |
| C | auto-B, independent auto-refinement | >= -10 A^2 | PASS | INCONCLUSIVE |

At 95% confidence, native CUDA retains **at least 99.97%** and the all-FFTW hybrid **at least 99.99%** of the effective data the CPU reference recovers — roughly 0.0001 A of equivalent resolution on a Rosenthal-Henderson basis. The same `default` outputs fail the 0.001 relative-image-RMSE limit 24/24 in #36's comparator. Both facts are true; they measure different things, which is what this issue asked to separate.

Stage B is the matched controlled diagnostic: 4452 particles, coordinates, orientations, origins, CTF, `rlnRandomSubset`, mask, box and symmetry all imported from this dataset's own RELION 5.0 tutorial precalculated project and held byte-identical across arms — verified, with the six arms' particle stacks giving six distinct digests while their metadata gives one shared digest `d54438c50f9b83f8` and all six post-processing runs randomising from the same 16.768418 A. Only the corrected micrograph differs. No motion re-estimation or polishing was run anywhere, so nothing later can mask the corrected-output difference. Unit of replication is the **movie** (delete-one jackknife, n = 22), never the pixel.

### The controls decide whether any of the above means anything

- **Sensitivity.** Adding noise at 5% of micrograph variance is resolved at **5.8 SE** (`rho` = 0.967); at 20% it gives `rho` = 0.878. The primary endpoint can see its own margin.
- **Specificity, and the direct answer to this issue's premise.** A deterministic `B = 20 A^2` envelope removes **81% of the power in the 3-2 A band** and 35% at 6-4 A, yet leaves FSC and resolution **unchanged** (`rho` = 1.004, `d143` delta = 0.000 A) while moving the auto-sharpening B by -20.5 A^2. A large corrected-image difference does not imply lost signal, and the B-factor endpoint tracks envelope shape rather than information content.
- **Honest negatives.** `CtfMaxResolution` moved by **-0.019 A** under the 20% noise control — i.e. it cannot detect a gross degradation on dose-weighted micrographs, so its PASS carries little information. `CtfFigureOfMerit` responds correctly (-3.5% at f=0.05, -12.7% at f=0.20) but the -5% margin is not tight enough to flag the 5% control. Stage A is a screen; Stage B carries the claim.

### Two things worth flagging to #36 / #58 / #60

1. **The hybrid's two-movie result does not extend to 24.** From #36's own comparator on the completed run: `allfftw` relative image RMSE spans 0.00046-0.00302 across 24 movies with **12 PASS / 12 FAIL** at the unchanged 0.001 limit, against 0.00062 / 0.00039 for `00021` / `00046`. That is #36's and #58's call; recorded here only because those outputs are this study's input.
2. **Per-movie image RMSE does not predict per-movie CTF-fit difference.** `r = -0.18` (`default`) vs `r = +0.40` (`allfftw`) against `|delta CtfMaxResolution|`; `-0.31` vs `+0.36` against `|delta defocus|`. n = 22, neither distinguishable from zero, sign flips between arms.
3. **Held-out 22 (3.124 A) beats all 24 (3.218 A)** by three Fourier shells despite 357 more particles — adding `00021` and `00046` makes the map worse. Another reason not to let those two movies carry a claim.

### A correction I made mid-study

The first Stage C pass was **discarded**. RELION's default `--random_seed` is time-derived, so the three arms were refined under different seeds — backend confounded with seed. Rerunning one arm under an explicit seed moved its resolution by a full Fourier shell, so the confound was not negligible. Stage C was rerun with the seed fixed and identical across arms and replicated over three seeds. Within-arm seed-driven spread in `d143` reaches 0.062 A, larger than any between-arm difference, so Stage C cannot resolve below ~0.06 A and every observed difference sits at or under its own noise floor. The discarded pass is retained in the results JSON.

### What this does not establish

One specimen, one collection, one detector. **No independent second collection exists on the project hosts**, and the held-out split within one collection is not a substitute — this is the main limit on generalisation. Stage B's FSC is comparative, not absolute, because orientations are imported. Stage A fits dose-weighted sums (the consumed arms used neither `--save_noDW` nor `--grouping_for_ps`), which costs power, not validity. Polishing, per-arm CTF in the reconstruction, picking sensitivity, a movie-level jackknife for Stage C, and all multi-worker / multi-GPU / non-5x5 configurations are declared **UNRUN** in a dedicated table. Point estimates favouring an accelerated arm are reported but **not** claimed as improvements — the design has no power for superiority and no superiority margin was set. **No gate threshold is proposed, evaluated or changed.**

### Compute

All on `4GPUs` under top-level `taskset -c 96-103` and `flock /tmp/motioncorr-bench.lock`, one phase at a time. **No MotionCorr run was launched** — all three arms were consumed from #36's completed artifacts. 244 `relion_reconstruct`, 122 `relion_postprocess` and 9 `relion_refine_mpi` runs, zero failures; ~35 min CPU batches plus 57 min of GPU refinement. Cross-host staging to `cpu64` measured 0.66 MB/s (57 MB in 86 s), which is why the 2.7 GB of accelerated-arm artifacts stayed where they were produced; the 8-CPU cap and single-job mutex were honoured throughout. RELION 5.1.0-commit-cb2683, byte-identical on both hosts.

### Addendum: independent convergence with #60

[PR #64](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/64) (#60) reaches the same conclusion from the opposite direction, which is worth recording explicitly because #58 needs both.

- **#60, forward from perturbation physics:** relative RMSE 0.001 corresponds to ~0.017 A^2 of envelope loss (~300x stricter than a 5 A^2 harm boundary); a 1-part-per-million gain-reference change already reads 2x the limit; the response saturates, so relative RMSE behaves as a near-binary "the arithmetic is not bit-identical" detector, and negligible- and unacceptable-tier distributions overlap 80x.
- **#61, backward from downstream outcome:** the `default` outputs that fail that limit 24/24 retain >= 99.97% of the effective data CPU recovers (95% lower bound, movie-level jackknife, n = 22), on endpoints demonstrated to resolve a known 5% loss at 5.8 SE.

Two independent methods, no shared machinery beyond the same 24 movies, agreeing that the 0.001 relative-RMSE result carries no information about scientific quality. Neither study proposes a replacement limit — that stays with #58, and both are inputs to it rather than arguments for any particular value.

Recorded in the report at `ef5935e`.

<!-- mc-audit-verified-20260927-issue61 -->
## Agent handoff: preserve the completed one-collection study and its limits

PR65 (`ef5935e`) contains the prospective tutorial-collection study. Its held-out movies are from the same collection; they are not independent detector/specimen validation. #73 owns that separate question. Do not rerun or rewrite this study merely to relabel it with today's main SHA.

### Review tasks
1. Compare the registered protocol/margin with the actual analysis and source/input manifests. Separate frozen-model signal diagnostics from independently refined downstream outcomes and list what each endpoint can detect.
2. Verify complete movie/particle/half-set accounting, matched masks/settings, harmful controls and reported uncertainty. Unit-of-analysis must match the inference; millions of correlated pixels are not millions of independent experimental replicates.
3. Preserve CPU, native CUDA and hybrid labels and all numerical diagnostics. A scientific noninferiority result does not retroactively pass an image-RMSE gate or prove operational reliability.
4. Check the PR diff is research/tooling/evidence only. Retain pinned historic artifacts or extract them narrowly onto current main without importing unrelated old source. Append fresh verification records only for work actually rerun.
5. Publish a bounded completion recommendation for this study with explicit endpoint/collection limitations. Feed its result to #18/#83 as scientific evidence and leave independent generality in #73.

### Next study, only if separately undertaken
Freeze the current candidate, dataset selection and scientifically meaningful margin before examining new held-out outcomes. Keep later polishing/motion re-estimation from silently masking the correction differences being evaluated. Report pass/fail/inconclusive and sensitivity controls; no margin fitted to make the candidate pass.

No production kernel/gate change, default promotion or large acquisition is authorized by this comment. Follow #66's compute/evidence contract; #60 owns diagnostic calibration.

body:
## Outcome reversed on review: Stage B verdicts withdrawn to INCONCLUSIVE

Following the Codex and Copilot reviews of [PR #65](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/65) at `ef5935e`, and a second review round on the fixes themselves, **the non-inferiority conclusion I posted on 2026-09-25 does not stand.** Full disposition in the [PR thread](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/65); the substance for this issue:

### What was wrong

The validity precondition claimed the endpoint could resolve its harm margin because `ctrl_noise_f005` sat 5.8 SE from `rho = 1.0`. It did not: that control measured `rho = 0.9666` and **passed** the 0.95 margin, so it never exercised the decision the endpoint makes. I added four margin-calibrated controls and a criterion **S1** — "no control at or beyond the margin may earn a PASS" — and reported it demonstrated at `rho = 0.94914`.

**S1 is vacuous.** A one-sided lower bound satisfies `lower95 <= rho` by construction, so any control classified harmful by its measured `rho` can never pass; the criterion could not fail. It has content only for a margin-designed control whose measured `rho` lands *above* the margin, and none did.

That leaves only positive rejection, demonstrated at `rho = 0.9146` — an 8.5% effective-data loss, not the 5% margin. **Sensitivity at the prespecified harm margin is unproven**, so every Stage B verdict for `default` and `allfftw` is withdrawn from PASS to INCONCLUSIVE under [Amendment 2](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/feat/issue-61-scientific-noninferiority/docs/issue61_noninferiority/PROTOCOL.md#10-amendments).

### Revised answer to this issue's pass criteria

| Stage | Endpoint | `default` | `allfftw` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | CTF max resolution / defocus / FoM | PASS* | PASS* |
| **B** | **effective-data fraction `rho`** | **INCONCLUSIVE** | **INCONCLUSIVE** |
| B | `d143`, auto-B | INCONCLUSIVE | INCONCLUSIVE |
| C | `d143`, auto-B after independent refinement | PASS** | PASS** / INCONCLUSIVE |

\* Stage A's own controls show it cannot detect a 5% loss, and CTF max resolution does not move even under a 20% one.
\*\* Stage C has **no positive control at all**, and its within-arm seed spread (0.062 Å) exceeds every between-arm difference it measured.

**No prespecified endpoint supports a non-inferiority conclusion for either backend.** That is a statement about the evidence, not about the backends.

### What does still stand

- Both accelerated arms are **measurably indistinguishable from CPU at the precision achieved**: observed effective-data loss 4.1e-5 and 1.9e-5, bounds 162x and 610x inside the allowed loss, under a matched design now verified field-by-field (18 named fields, 6 arms, 144 stacks, one shared metadata digest).
- The endpoint **does** detect an 8.5% loss and tracks four designed degradation levels quantitatively — it is not inert.
- The specificity result is unaffected and remains the sharpest thing here: a deterministic envelope removing **81% of 3-2 Å power** leaves FSC and resolution **unchanged**. Image difference does not imply signal loss. This still converges with #60's independent finding that the 0.001 relative-RMSE limit is a near-binary "not bit-identical" detector.
- No measurement changed. Every endpoint value, bound and all 72 pixel digests reproduce exactly. **No margin, threshold or gate was relaxed** — both amendments are tightenings, and the second removes a conclusion.

### The one experiment that would resolve it

≥20 independent noise realisations of a margin-designed control (`f = 0.062`), full jackknife each, counting how many wrongly yield `lower95 >= 0.95`; plus a replicate set at the real arms' precision scale (`SE ~ 1.6e-4` vs `~8e-3`). ≈920 reconstructions + 460 post-processing runs, ~50 min of exclusive `cpu64` lock. **Not run** — it is a design-validation study rather than a review fix, so I have left the decision to you.

Compute: `cpu64` cores 32-63 / NUMA node 1, ≤12 concurrent, behind the issue-96 validation lock, `ctffind` untouched, no GPU and no SCARF allocation. Read-only passes on `4GPUs` used cores 120-123, outside both reservations. Not merging or closing.

Data point for this study, from #171 (experimental `--fft_size_policy fast`: 7-smooth padded FFTs, hidden and off by default).

**Speed:** 96 movies 25.88 → 22.64 s (−13.4%), 24 movies 7.19 → 6.13 s (−12.6%). Products differ, so these are speed-only verdicts.

**Validation against the CPU reference, existing gates unchanged:** it fails.

| what is padded | movies passing | worst image RMSE (gate 0.02) | max local trajectory change |
|---|---|---|---|
| nothing (default) | 24/24 | 0.009 | 0.065 px |
| frames and patches | 0/24 | 0.049 | 0.72 px |
| frames only | 0/24 | 0.046 | 0.74 px |
| patches only | 3/24 | 0.038 | 0.36 px |

**Where the error comes from:**
- **Frame padding** replaces the periodic wrap at the image edges with mean fill: 58% of the squared error is in the outer 8 px.
- **Patch padding** changes the fitted local motion model by up to 0.36 px.
- Dose weighting is not the cause.

**The current gates are also too coarse to validate a mode like this.** A dose-weight grid wrong by 1% of each axis falls below their resolution. Any future non-identical speed mode needs finer, calibrated gates first (#60).
